reason: E1 supports the strength-ductility benefit of coherent nanoprecipitates in W-based HEAs, but neither E1 nor E2 provides any evidence for copper addition, Cu-rich nanoprecipitate formation, or enhanced thermal conductivity in these systems. The cited evidence is thus only loosely related to the core premises.
premises: Coherent nanoprecipitates can simultaneously enhance strength and ductility in refractory HEAs.
Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitation (SCCP) is a viable processing route for such alloys.
Refractory HEAs like (CrFeTiTa)70W30 are suitable baseline interlayer materials for divertor applications.
Copper addition can form coherent Cu-rich nanoprecipitates within a refractory HEA matrix.
Coherent Cu nanoprecipitates will significantly boost thermal conductivity without degrading mechanical integrity.
